OMG I'VE FOUND MY NEW OBSESSION. This is everything I wanted in a book and more. Ahh I didn't want to stop reading and didn't want the book to end 😩 The perfect sort of book to get one out of a slump and give the cozy, warm paranormal vibes- just more intense.

It's got a good world building. The pacing is fast and straight to the point, there's not much filler in it and I absolutely loved it. Cause not all books need to be 500+ pages thick. This was just under and got everything done beautifully. The political intrigue between the wolves and humans was so interesting to me. And omg the drama 🤭🤭

The characters are pretty likable and complex. I loved Aurora as the fmc, she's got fire in her and strong with her opinions and yet there was an innocence about her which I appreciated. Callum is so easy to like. He's the kind of guy or rather wolf you cuddle, who's warm and straightforward. He's simplistic in his ideals and I loved that about him. His possessiveness and protective side was endearing. Blake, on the other hand, is more cunning, subtle. I loved his manipulative and dark self. Basically, he's like Rhysand from ACOTAR- not acomaf- just to be clear. Iykyk 👀🤭

The chemistry is so good between them. The dynamics just work perfectly. The romance between Callum and Aurora is sweet, hot and swoon worthy. They had me blushing, giggling and kicking my feet. But I want to see some Blake in the mix, cause I just know that man is going to shake my world if I do get his scenes in a more romantic or spicy fashion.

The ending had me shook. I couldn't put the book down at all. Some of the things were a bit predictable, I won't lie. But at the same time, I ate it all up. The action and twists were so good. I can't wait to read the next book.

Basically, go read it if you're in the mood for sone werewolves. It won't disappoint 👀🤭

Maybe it’s the aftermath of my overdosing Wattpad werewolf teen phase (no regrets—those days were a blast!), but now, I'm yearning for something with a touch more elegance. To my surprise, this book was written by the same author of Cupid's Match, which ultimately is one of my favorites Wattpad story back then. Unfortunately, this one didn’t quite capture the same magic I was hoping for, and nostalgia just wasn’t enough to save it.

I definitely appreciate the short chapters from the book, which should make for a breezy read, but instead, they stretch the story thin, spinning in place without progression. Multiple chapters pass, yet the plot remains static, looping the same uneventful moment without momentum. The narration meanders and my interest waned with every digression.

Now that I am looking back, I’ve noticed Palphreyman has a habit of shoehorning love triangles into her work—a trope I have outgrown as maturity has shown me how rarely it’s done well. Most of the time, it’s just hollow drama for drama’s sake and sadly, this book is no exception. Neither of the love interest stands out to me: Callum is blandly chivalrous, while Blake’s constant smirking and faux mystery make him more grating than intriguing. Their dynamic isn’t a conflict but rather a filler to stretch a flimsy plot across future installments.

And so, it’s genuinely disappointing how this novel squander its promising beginning. The moment Aurora enters the wolf kingdom; the story loses all pace. We’re subjected to endless cycles of the same internal monologues, with key motivations rehashed in nearly identical wording chapter after chapter. The dialogue serves only as exposition, and the chapters lack satisfying arcs, often ending abruptly.

A teenage me, who once gobbled up anything on the orange app, might’ve devoured this. Now? The author's writing feels frozen in time—unchallenged, unrefined, and painfully surface-level. There’s no richness to the world, no complexity to the characters, just a void shell of a story that leaves me wondering why I bothered. A disappointing execution of what could have been a compelling premise.

I NEED TO BE A DETECTIVE FIRST.



If there’s one thing these romantasy books have taught me, it’s this: I NEVER root for the blond man. Never. (Okay, maybe there are exceptions, but let’s be serious… not this time.)



And listen — I might be shooting in the dark here, but I really don’t think so considering I figured out the “plot twist” by chapter two.

So naturally, I gathered evidence.

⚠️If you want to play detective yourself, SKIP THIS PART NOW.⚠️

EXHIBIT A:
“His name is Blake. He’s the most dangerous male in the Kingdom of Wolves, and he has the power to help us… or destroy us.”

EXCUSE ME, MISS???
Why are you NOT already climbing that man like a tree???


EXHIBIT B:
“…he’s dressed in dark breeches rather than a kilt, and wears a black shirt perfectly fitted to his hard chest and torso. His hair is dark…”

IF BAD, WHY HOT???

EXHIBIT C:
“A slow smile spreads across Blake's face and dimples puncture his cheeks.”

DIMPLES??????
OH SO WE’RE JUST HANDING OUT WEAPONS NOW???
You thought I WOULDN’T notice the dimples? Amateur behavior.

EXHIBIT D:
“He surprises me by crouching on one knee before me. He picks up the collar, then looks up.”

Do I even NEED to continue?
Because personally, I did enjoy the sight of you kneeling.


EXHIBIT E:
“He smells like night, like the most dangerous part of the forest, like dark forbidden places.”

Ma’am.
MA’AM.
That is not a red flag. That is a marriage proposal.

EXHIBIT F:
“The shadows seem to curl around me. They protect me.”

MMMMMMMMHMMMMMM GIRL.
TAKE THE HINT.

And no, I will NOT apologize for entering full detective mode because this book was NOT subtle. Like at all. Which is honestly why this is a 4-star read instead of a 5-star read…
BUT DON’T GET IT TWISTED.
Even though I figured out the plot twist within the first 15 minutes, I STILL ate this up. Licked the plate clean. No crumbs left. I was INVESTED.



This book felt like watching Love Island with wolves. The vibes? VIBING. The possessiveness? Delicious. The jealousy outbursts? Spectacular. The emotionally constipated wolf-man behavior simmering beneath the surface? Inject it directly into my bloodstream.

Callum, sweetheart… you are cute. You are lovely. You are emotionally available.
Which is unfortunately exactly why you were never going to win.
I mean, don’t get me wrong — I would’ve folded for him too. IMMEDIATELY. But this is romantasy. Nice men finish second.



And Aurora??? My girl went from shy little miss “oh no” to whispering stuff like “take your pleasure from me” and I was LOSING MY MIND 😭😭😭
Her discovering her sexuality was genuinely the funniest and most entertaining thing ever. I was cackling. I was cheering. I was deeply unwell.

Anyway.
Jumping into book two immediately.

Werewolves with Scottish accents and kilts? Yes, please!

I haven’t read a romantasy in quite a while, and this one ended up being the perfect palate cleanser. I’m all for a smutty read, but in this genre, I much prefer stories with an actual plot rather than ones that rely solely on the spice, which this one balanced really well.

I started with the audiobook, and while I loved listening to Shane East’s swoon worthy narration of Callum, Zara Hampton-Brown’s narration of Aurora felt overly dramatic to me. She rarely sounded natural and always seemed breathy or anxious, which became tiresome pretty quickly, so I eventually switched over to my Kindle.

I feel a love triangle brewing, which I’m not quite sure how I feel about, but I’m definitely curious to see how the dynamics shift in the next installment. It sure would be nice if Libby would hand over book two today as a little Mother’s Day gift to me.

Rating: 4.5 stars.
“I want you to smell like me. When another wolf is close, I want it to be my scent they smell on your skin. I want to mark you as mine.”
Is it ACOTAR with werewolves? Absolutely.
Did I devour every single page of it? Without a doubt.

There’s just something irresistibly addictive about a story where a girl is torn from her world and thrust into another, one filled with danger, magic, and impossible choices. Aurora’s journey from a sheltered princess to a woman caught in the middle of a supernatural war had that perfect blend of tension, romance, and discovery that I can never get enough of.

And then there are the men, two powerful, magnetic forces pulling her in different directions. The brooding alpha with his secrets and scars, the kind of man who makes you question everything you thought you knew about monsters… and the human world she left behind, full of its own brand of cruelty. That love triangle, that emotional tug-of-war, it just works. Every. Single. Time.

The story balances action and emotion so well: brutal battles, simmering attraction, moral conflicts, and moments of vulnerability that sneak up on you. It’s dark and thrilling, but also deeply romantic in that “I shouldn’t want you, but I do” way that makes your heart ache.
So yes, if ACOTAR met a werewolf war and had a slow-burn, forbidden romance baby, this would be it, and I ate up every delicious, dramatic, dangerous page.


➺ The Characters:
Aurora:
“I’ll learn to fight. I’ll make my own stories, rather than be the side character in the stories of kings.”
The characters in The Wolf King are what make this story come alive, each one feels real, layered, and full of emotion, and they give the story a heartbeat that keeps you completely hooked. Aurora, especially, stole my heart. She’s fierce, passionate, and unafraid to stand up for herself, but there’s also this tender, vulnerable side to her that makes her so relatable. She’s not your typical damsel in distress, she’s figuring herself out in a world that constantly tries to control her, and you can feel every struggle, every moment of doubt, every spark of courage.

The chemistry between all of them? Chef’s kiss. The romance between Aurora and Callum had me absolutely kicking my feet, it’s sweet, hot, and brimming with emotion. Their connection feels organic and sincere, full of those tender, blush-inducing moments that make you squeal and reread lines twice.

Callem:
“I thought of you every hour I was away,” he says. “All I could think of was getting back to you. I shouldn’t have left you. I won’t do it again.”
And then there’s Callum, oh my heart, where do I even begin? He’s the kind of person who feels like a safe harbor in the middle of a storm, like when you see him, every chaos will be forgotten (he is going to be on my boyfriends list as well, hehe). There’s a loyalty and protectiveness about him that’s impossible not to fall for, the kind that makes you want to lean into him and never let go. His possessiveness doesn’t feel controlling at all, it’s instinctive, fierce, and full of care, the kind that makes your chest ache in the best way. He’s simple in his values, but that simplicity is comforting, like a quiet promise that even in a harsh, unpredictable world, love can still feel steady and real.
“I love him,” I say, softly. “I cannot marry you, because I love Callum.”
The one thing that really frustrated me about him was how every single time he went off to make some deal or handle his “king” duties, he left Aurora behind, and of course, every time he left, something would happen to her! Like, whyyyy?! It made me so anxious and honestly a little mad at him, because you just want him to stay and protect the person he clearly cares about. It was one of those moments that made me shout at the book like, “Stay with her, man! it’s getting annoying.”

Blake:
Ohhh, Blake… where do I even start?! My heart was literally racing every time he appeared on the page. He’s dark, dangerous, and just… magnetic in a way that makes you gasp and go, “Wait, why am I feeling this?!” His cunning, his subtle manipulations, that glint of danger in his eyes, it all makes your pulse spike like crazy. You know he’s bad for Aurora (and honestly, for you too if we’re being real), but somehow you can’t look away.

He’s got that irresistible Rhysand energy, mysterious, commanding, with a bite that makes your stomach twist in the best way. Every scene he’s in, I was sitting there clutching the book, heart pounding, whispering “oh no… oh yes…!” I swear, I lived for every single moment with him.


“I’ve wanted you since the moment I first set eyes on you. I told myself I took you from the Borderlands because I needed you for the Heart of the Moon, but I think even then, I knew the truth. I couldn’t bear the thought of leaving you there. And I wanted you. Goddess, I wanted you. I’ve been like a lovesick pup since that moment. I think about you all the time. I want to make you smile, and make you happy, and to impress you.”
Uhh… big, hot Scottish wolf-men? Yes please.
Sure, the story has its flaws, a few moments that made me pause or roll my eyes just a little, but honestly? I didn’t care. I was far too busy falling for Callum (and, if I’m completely honest, for Blake too). There’s something about their strength, their loyalty, that wild edge barely kept in check, it’s impossible not to get swept up in it.
“I thought you said there was always a choice. And what? You chose him?” His voice is dark, and his breathing shallow. “Did he touch you?”
This book gave me everything I wanted: danger, tension, heat, and that hint of tenderness buried under all the growling and chaos. It’s not perfect, but it’s fun, it’s addictive, and it makes you dream just a little about having your own brooding wolf-man waiting in the shadows. Just read it, let go of logic for a while, and enjoy the ride.

“I won’t, Rory. I promise I will not ask you to do anything that will cause you harm, nor compromise your morals or integrity. And in return, while you will be mine, I will be yours, too. I will be your alpha. And I promise to take care of you. For as long as you’re here, with me.”


➺ World Building:
The werewolf lore in The Wolf King really strikes that perfect balance between the familiar and the unexpected. I especially loved how the story explored politics on two paces, the regal, courtly kind tied to Aurora’s world, and the primal, instinct-driven power plays among the wolves. It made the stakes feel so much bigger than just romance (though the romance definitely burns). The moral grayness throughout, no clear “good” or “bad” side, gave it an emotional weight that really pulled me in.
If anything, I just wanted more of it. More detail about how the territories interact, how the clans formed, what their customs mean. There’s so much potential in this world that I hope the next book dives even deeper into. Still, as a first installment, it did exactly what it needed to: built a vivid foundation, set up political intrigue, and left me hungry for the next chapter.


The ending completely shook me, I was on the edge of my seat until the very last page and honestly could not put the book down. Every twist, every reveal kept me glued to the story, my heart racing with each turn. Sure, there were moments that frustrated me, like some of Rory’s decisions that made me want to scream at the pages, but even those moments added to the intensity of the story and made it feel more real, I guess.

The action was relentless and thrilling, with danger around every corner, and the emotional stakes were just as high. I loved how the author balanced high-octane tension with the slow-burn romance and character development. By the time I reached the final chapters, I was completely invested in the characters and their fates, desperate to see how everything would play out.

Now, all I can do jump immediately into the next book. I’m beyond excited to dive back into this world, explore more of the pack dynamics, and finally see how the relationships and conflicts evolve. The Wolf King left me both breathless and hungry for more, and I can’t wait to get back into the chaos, passion, and drama of this gripping series.


── .✦

༉‧₊🕯️🖤❀༉ Omg, like… I’ve been watching people LOSING THEIR MINDS over this book, sobbing, gasping, feral giggling, the whole dramatic package, and I’m officially done playing it cool. I NEED to know what’s going on in those pages. This is officially my first dark romantasy (send prayers pls), and I’m equal parts scared and absolutely pumped. I want the morally gray chaos, the intense yearning, the emotional damage, WHATEVER it is that’s turning everyone else into unhinged book gremlins.
So yeah… if this book ruins my life in the best way possible, just know I walked in willingly. Let’s do this.

OKAY OKAY, I AM OBSESSED!! This book must be laced with some sort of illegal substance because it had me ADDICTED to flipping the pages even faster than I'd flip over for a certain alpha.

The world building? Superb! The descriptions of the environment and surroundings provided a welcomed sense of immersive cosiness within an otherwise intense and angsty paranormal romance.

The tension? DELICIOUS! And is that a love triangle I smell? I am hooked!

I'll be honest, during the first half of the book, Aurora kind of irritated me. I totally get that as a princess she has been sheltered her entire life and schooled on what is "proper", but her naivety and immaturity towards certain things, although very true to character, was kind of frustrating. HOWEVER, I loved her character development. The way she became a total badass and wasn't afraid to stand up for herself by biting back at people pushing her around or treating her undesirably was so refreshing!

I love a possessive MMC, so I really liked Callum and his soft yet protective personality. The tension between him and Aurora was palpable and I totally ate it up! However, Blake has my FULL ATTENTION! 👀 Every appearance he made had me kicking my feet and giggling. As much as I liked Callum, I think his vibe was slightly too golden retriever-esque for me. Blake on the other hand, shared the same "alpha male, touch her and die" vibes, but also had an air of aloofness, which, quite frankly I found rather hot. If you've read any of my other romance reviews, you will know that I LOVE a dark, morally grey mmc, and Blake fitted that to a T!

I've read a few reviews where people have pointed out similarities to the vibes in the ACOTAR series, especially drawing on resemblances between Blake and Rhysand.. and honestly, I have to agree! But lemme say right now, if the Callum/Blake sitch turns into a Tamlin/Rhysand sitch, I fear I may lose my mind (not that I'll be complaining, I am HERE for the drama!). Is this gonna be a "fight for the girl" vibe? Is it gonna be more of a "why choose" moment? I don't know, but I NEED TO FIND OUT!

Now let's talk about that ending. Yes, I guessed part of the plot twist from early on and found elements a little predictable, but that CLIFFHANGER had me launching my book across the room, screaming into my pillow, chewing on my hand, booking the next flight to Scotland and changing my name to "Lauren Palphreyman's #1 enemy" because what do you MEAN you're going to end the book on such a diabolical cliffhanger!? I am FERAL, I tell you!! I cannot wait to dive into The Night Prince and find out what happens next!

Can I just say this has hot werewolf shifters with SCOTTISH ACCENTS! I COULD NOT PUT THIS DOWN!!!

Gosh, I loved this. I genuinely could have read it in one sitting.

This is one of those books where there is absolutely not a single slow moment. From the very first scene, I was completely hooked. The world felt rich and immersive without ever slowing the pacing, and every scene just kept raising the stakes higher and higher.

And the romance??? I don’t know if it was because I was ovulating or what, but this made me absolutely feral. CALLUM??? The perfect blend of dangerous, commanding, and devastatingly magnetic. The way he treated Aurora had me falling right along with her. Every interaction between them was laced with intensity, and the chemistry was completely off the charts. The slow build, the power dynamics, the emotional payoff—it was all executed flawlessly. I really hope he never gets his heart broken. However, if I learned anything from ACOTAR it is that you never freaking know LOL!

This book truly had everything: Scottish, overprotective, insanely hot werewolf shifters, tension, YEARNING, witty banter, and an absolutely lovable cast of characters. I also really appreciated how well-balanced it was—there was a perfect mix of romance, action, and character development.

And listen—I’ve said it before and I’ll say it again, I’m not really a “just romance and spice” kind of reader. I need plot, and this delivered a very juicy one.

That ending had me on the edge of my seat, and I am so happy I already have the next book because there is no way I could wait after that. Also… Blake??? He definitely has my attention, and I am very excited to see more of him in book two.

Absolutely obsessed. 100% recommend✨

you know what... HELL YEAHHH!

This was one wild ride from start to finish and I ate up every single second of it 💃🐺 Why have I never read any werewolf books before?? I have been missing out 😩 This was scrumptious 🤌

This had a fast plot and great world building. It also had short chapters... like that's what I'm talking about 💃💃 I don't think I was bored for even a second of this book. The author described this world perfectly without getting too over the top and detailed about it, which was so refreshing and easy.

Aurora was a very likeable fmc and I loved her fiery side. She was a tad bit annoying at the start with her willingness to just go along with a bunch of wolves kidnapping her but yk whatever... water under the bridge at this point 😭 She's stubborn and not afraid to give people a piece of her mind and I was all here for it 🤭

Callum is the perfect golden retriever man (*ahem* or should I say wolf🐺). Simple and safe. I had some problems with him though. One being him saying many times "I'll never let anyone touch you again." and then leaving her in the middle of the woods on her own to go find them breakfast 😭 like dude... what did you think was going to happen?? Also, I can't lie the kilt got me every single time, I just couldn't help but let out a little laugh (I mean no disrespect to kilts though). Overall, he was really sweet and protective and had me swooning at times, so I'll give him that.

BLAKEEE! Obsessed would be an understatement. What can I say 🤷‍♀️ I'm a sucker for morally grey, guarded men 🙇‍♀️🙇‍♀️ His chemistry and tension with Aurora was off the charts!! Never knew I could like the nickname "Little rabbit" but here we are! 🤭 He had me giggling and kicking my feet every damn time. Let me just leave this right here ⬇️⬇️

"You look exquisite, by the way." "You should never pretend to be less than what you are."

I don't think I heard Callum say anything like that to her... just saying 😏

Although I found some things predictable, no one could have prepared me for that diabolical cliffhanger!!! My jaw is still somewhere on the floor... idk if I'll find it until I have book two in my hands 😭

✩ 4.5 stars ✩

What to Expect:
➼ Forced Proximity
➼ Political Intrigue
➼ Wolf Shifters
➼ Captured Princess
➼ Potential Love Triangle
➼ Reluctant Allies-to-Lovers
➼ One Horse
➼ Multiple Alphas
➼ Scottish Highland Setting/Characters
➼ Duet Narration by Zara Hampton-Brown & Shane East
➼ First Person Dual POV

This is exactly what I’m looking for in a Romantasy! 👏🏻

This is being described as ACOTAR meets Outlander with werewolves and that felt very accurate! The entry point into the story allowed the author to share a very clear picture of the FMC’s life prior to meeting the MMC and gave the reader a lot of insight into how the wolves (and women) were treated in their society. She is about to enter into an arranged marriage with a very bad man and it is clear that her future in the castle will not be a happy one if she stays. Callum is also aware of this fact and after she shows compassion to one of his wolves, he knows he can’t leave her behind. He also believes that she would be a very valuable chess piece to use to negotiate for the thing his people want most. This makes their relationship even more complex since he is both her captor AND her savior. He was really kind of a cinnamon roll while still being a possessive alpha male which was a great combo. He was definitely a little too loyal and trusting at times, but as MMC’s go, he was pretty perfect!

Basically, I loved every second of this, and now… I’m scared. 😂 (Potential Spoilers ahead) I’ve heard only good things about book two, but I HATED Blake and it’s very much looking like we’re heading into love triangle territory with him. The similarities between him and Rhysand are definitely there, which should be amazing news since he’s my all time favorite MMC, but Callum has just been too good up to this point for me to be on board with any type of shift.

I read a lot of fantasy though and it’s never a good sign when the MC’s are this happy in book one, so I’m at a point where I actually don’t think Callum will be end game at all… I’ve taken some time to sit with that possibility and now I think I might be ready to dive into The Night Prince. I swear, so many of my favorite books feature love triangles, but I still HATE to see them coming. I feel like I’ll probably end up loving it, but I’m not sure I’m ready! A throuple would be worse. Please no throuple. 🙅🏼‍♀️ If you know something about the next book, please don’t even hint at it in the comments. Some of you guys aren’t nearly as subtle as you think you are. 😅 No spoilers!

⋆˙⟡ 3.5 ⭐️ get comfy, besties - i have a lot of thoughts to unpack.

firstly, i’m pretty sure this is my first true shifter romance, which honestly feels like a milestone in itself. that being said, i’ve read enough books incorporating shifters that i had a decent idea of what to expect. in any case, the world-building was simple, but effective enough. it didn’t paint some rich tapestry of a foreign mystical land, but it absolutely delivered on the scottish / outlander vibes - and i, for one, will never complain about that (swoons aggressively for jamie fraser, iykyk).

the princess of the southlands - otherwise known as aurora. i shall call her princess, though, because honestly, how many times did she repeat, “i am the princess of the southlands”? the limit does not exist. if i had a dollar for every time she reminded us, i could probably fund the entire kingdom myself and buy her a new personality while i’m at it. the southlands princess better be a work in progress. because right now? we are working with very little. i swear this girl actually became progressively dumber as the book went on. nevertheless, i’ll give her another chance because apparently i enjoy naive fools.

callum might be the most patient man - or, as aurora would say, “male” - to exist within this world. old mate put up with aurora every damn day and somehow managed to do it with a smile. callum is the ultimate golden retriever in human form: loyal, sweet, and BORING. like, aggressively beige. i swear he started off interesting, or maybe that was just his narrator’s dreamy scottish accent, but somewhere between the endless princess declarations and the slow middle, callum quickly lost my interest.

nothing substantial really happened through the middle of the book. the main focus was the budding romance between aurora and callum *yawn*. i could have done with more of - you guessed it - BLAAAAKE. i seriously cannot keep track of the number of times people have collectively lost their minds over this man. the hype? astronomical. the expectations? through the roof. now i’ve finally met the man, the myth, the legend, and i’m standing here like… okay, i see the vision, but i need more.

i won’t lie, i’m intrigued, but blake hasn’t sold me just yet. maybe it was the absolute character assassination of having the female narrator voice his part in the audiobook, or maybe it was one too many lines about “playing games with the little rabbit.” either way, i’m told blake is narrated by sean masters in book two, so future me won’t even pretend to be unaffected.

i definitely have my gripes but, it was a fun time, and i’m excited to see where book two takes me. mostly because i need answers, a personality transplant for at least one character, and, most importantly, more blake.

⋆˙⟡ pre read → on my way to meet blakeee 💃🐺🐶

Read My Honest Book Review on My Blog:
The Wolf King

The romance felt more like emotional whiplash than a slow burn, and one possessive trope moment ultimately sealed my DNF. I wanted stronger character growth, clearer tension, and a relationship that felt more intentional.

This will work for readers who love possessive wolf shifter romantasy, and if you enjoyed Dire Bound, you might still want to give it a shot.
